workflow_scale_routing.rationale: One written artifact can hold the movement through text sections without long-work stewardship.
reroute_triggers: Artist requests dependent parts, a sequence or series, durable canon, or long-form drafting across sessions.

writing_method.rationale: The target is a reader-facing finished opinion article, so the cultural format shape should govern section planning while the Beat Plan governs emotional movement.

medium_output_shape_recommendation.rationale: The invented material has a timely civic claim, public stakes, accountable speaker, evidence, counterargument, and requested change.
tradeoffs: The op-ed shape favors persuasion over neutral explanation.
The compact length requires pointed evidence instead of exhaustive reporting.

cultural_format_structure.name: Op-Ed
cultural_format_structure.audience_promise: The reader will understand the speaker's public claim, why it matters now, why the speaker can responsibly make it, and what should change.
cultural_format_structure.audience_hook: Open with a concrete invented moment: a resident reaches a cooling center after a late shift and finds the doors closed.

parts.label: News hook or lede
parts.function: Shows why this argument matters now.

parts.label: Argument / thesis
parts.function: States or clearly implies the position.

parts.label: Authority
parts.function: Shows why the speaker is accountable to the claim.

parts.label: Evidence points
parts.function: Supports the argument with credible material.

parts.label: Counterargument
parts.function: Acknowledges a strong objection or limitation.

parts.label: Stakes
parts.function: Explains who is affected and why the issue matters.

parts.label: Close / call
parts.function: Ends with consequence, action, warning, or memorable observation.

cultural_format_structure.turn_or_payoff: The close should sharpen the public consequence: refusing a measured evening-hours pilot makes the city accountable for a protection people cannot reach.

invertible: Authority may appear before or after the thesis if the lede needs immediate grounding.

failure_modes: The piece has opinions but no argument.
The hook is timely but the thesis is generic.
Evidence is asserted rather than shown.
The counterargument is weak or caricatured.
The ending scolds instead of persuading.

text_form.rationale: The `op_ed` Cultural Format Structure is a subtype of article, and the existing enum does not need a dedicated op-ed value because the cultural format carries the subtype.
avoid: Do not turn the op-ed into a neutral explainer.
Do not add a separate article subtype enum unless downstream routing cannot distinguish `article` plus `op_ed`.

voice_point_of_view.speaker: A neighborhood tenant-help volunteer using invented civic experience.
voice_point_of_view.point_of_view: First-person plural used sparingly, with direct public argument in third-person policy language.
voice_point_of_view.distance: Close enough to show accountable proximity, restrained enough to avoid memoir.
voice_point_of_view.authority: Accountability comes from helping residents navigate services and observing access barriers.
voice_constraints: No real city, official, or private person names.
No invented statistics presented as verified fact.

structure_plan.structure_rationale: The section plan maps op-ed cultural-format parts to concrete drafting sections while preserving local section jobs and Beat Plan movement.

sections.section_job: Make the timing problem immediate through one safe invented moment, then name the public access gap.
sections.expectation_turn_translation: The text sets up an available public service, then reveals that its hours make it unavailable to the resident who needs it.
source_wording_notes: Avoid pretending the incident is a verified report.
sections.paragraph_distinction: Concrete moment and public urgency; no policy detail yet.

sections.section_job: State that the city should pilot evening cooling-center hours on heat-alert days and explain the speaker's accountable vantage point.
sections.intended_feeling: Trust in a specific, accountable claim
sections.expectation_turn_translation: The text shifts from complaint to a bounded testable remedy.
source_wording_notes: Keep authority tied to service navigation and observed access barriers.
sections.paragraph_distinction: Position and speaker accountability; not yet the evidence build.

sections.section_job: Show why daytime-only hours predictably miss shift workers, caretakers, and transit-dependent residents.
sections.expectation_turn_translation: Instead of expanding into a broad climate essay, the text narrows evidence to access mechanics.
source_wording_notes: Use qualitative invented examples clearly as rehearsal material.
sections.paragraph_distinction: Reasoned support; less anecdotal than the lede and more concrete than the thesis.

sections.section_job: Explain that the schedule excludes people whose work, caregiving, or transit constraints make evening access essential.
sections.expectation_turn_translation: The text turns formal availability into practical exclusion.
source_wording_notes: Keep affected residents generalized and respectful.
sections.paragraph_distinction: Human consequence; warmer and more grounded than the evidence paragraph.

sections.section_job: Acknowledge cost, staffing, and safety constraints, then answer with a limited pilot and measurement.
sections.expectation_turn_translation: The text treats the objection as real and lets it refine the policy instead of weakening the claim.
source_wording_notes: Do not caricature budget or staffing concerns.
sections.paragraph_distinction: Deliberately cooler and more analytical than the stakes section.

sections.section_job: Ask for the evening-hours pilot and end on the consequence of a public protection that closes before people can reach it.
sections.expectation_turn_translation: The text refuses a mere summary and makes inaction harder to defend.
source_wording_notes: Avoid adding new evidence in the final paragraph.
sections.paragraph_distinction: Memorable consequence and call; firmer than the counterargument, cleaner than the lede.

length_policy.rationale: A compact op-ed should be long enough for evidence and counterargument but short enough to keep the public claim sharp.

source_wording_constraints: All material is safe invented rehearsal content.
transformation_allowed: Compress invented notes into an argument.
Create fresh wording from the rehearsal Artist Meaning.
Reorder op-ed parts when needed for clarity while preserving all required parts.
fidelity_policy.rights_notes: Disposable dry-run artifact; no user-provided private media or generated work is included.
fidelity_policy.rationale: The rehearsal tests structure mapping, not preservation of a real Reference's wording.

publication_use.audience: General public readers of a local opinion page.
publication_use.privacy_notes: No real people, locations, or private facts are used.
publication_use.rights_notes: Safe invented material only; no provider generation.

traceability_summary.note: The plan preserves the invented meaning: practical access matters more than symbolic service availability.
Each section maps to a Beat Plan beat and key emotional movement.
The op-ed shape is accepted for rehearsal without artist confirmation.
